name: Seoul Museum of History
summary: Free, modern museum tracing Seoul's growth from Joseon capital to megacity, with a walk-on glass city model.
description: A well-funded municipal museum next to Gyeonghuigung Palace, telling Seoul's history from the 1394 founding to today through full-scale street recreations, a giant illuminated city model you walk over on glass flooring, and free English audio guides. Exhibits are air-conditioned, spacious, and easy for a group of five to move through at their own pace. The permanent galleries take about 1.5-2 hours; families can skim faster. English signage is strong throughout.
highlights: Glass-floor walkway over the illuminated Seoul city model
Full-scale 1950s-60s Seoul streetscape reconstruction
Free English audio guide (leave an ID)
tips: Free admission, free water, free audio guide with ID deposit
Guided English-friendly tours run Tue-Sat from 11am
Pair with adjacent Gyeonghuigung Palace grounds for a free afternoon

reviews.text: Fantastic free museum - learned so much about how Seoul developed, with great English explanations.

name: Haneul Park (Sky Park)
summary: Flat-topped former landfill turned open grassland park with a huge Han River and city skyline view, best at sunset.
description: Part of World Cup Park in Sangam-dong, Haneul Park sits on a reclaimed former garbage landfill capped with grass and, from mid-September through November, waves of silver pampas grass. The plateau is flat and paved-path accessible (a shuttle bus runs up from the base for those who don't want the short climb), opening onto one of Seoul's widest unobstructed skyline and Han River views. Arrive toward sunset for the best light and to stay through early dusk when the city lights come on.
highlights: Silver grass fields (best late Sep-Nov)
360-degree Han River and skyline view
Windmill photo point and sunset benches
tips: A small shuttle bus climbs the hill for visitors who don't want the 10-15 min walk up
Come 30-45 min before sunset and stay for the after-dark skyline

name: Gyeongui Line Forest Park (Yeonnam-dong)
summary: A converted railway line turned skinny green park through Yeonnam-dong's cafe and brunch streets, nicknamed 'Yeontral Park'.
description: Built over a decommissioned rail line, this ribbon of lawn and trees runs through Hongdae/Yeonnam-dong and is flanked by some of Seoul's best brunch cafes, bakeries, and boutiques. Locals picnic on the grass on weekends; the flat, paved path is easy for the whole family and connects straight into Hongik University Street. It's an easy, low-effort stroll rather than an attraction with an entrance, ideal for filling an afternoon between meals.

name: Deoksugung Stone Wall Path
summary: A gingko-lined lane hugging Deoksugung Palace's old stone wall, one of Seoul's most photographed short walks.
description: This easy 10-minute stroll follows the granite wall of Deoksugung Palace between City Hall and Jeong-dong, shaded by mature gingko and plane trees that turn gold in autumn. It requires no admission, no stairs, and no real walking effort - just a pleasant loop past cafes, small galleries, and the Seoul Museum of Art annex. Popular with couples and easy to combine with the palace itself or Seoul City Hall/Library next door.
highlights: Stone wall and gingko canopy
Views into Deoksugung Palace grounds
Connects directly to Seoul City Hall Plaza
tips: Best light is late afternoon; gingko turns gold from mid-October, still green in late Sep
Completely flat and stroller-friendly

name: National Assembly Building
summary: South Korea's domed parliament building on Yeouido, free to tour with advance reservation, plus riverside park grounds.
description: A green-domed 1975 landmark on Yeouido overlooking the Han River, the National Assembly Building offers free self-guided or reserved tours through its main hall, lobby, and an exhibition on Korean democracy. The wide plaza and pond out front are pleasant even without a tour, and the building anchors Yeouido Hangang Park just a short walk away. It's a low-effort, air-conditioned stop that works well combined with a Han River walk.

name: Culture Station Seoul 284
summary: The restored 1925 Renaissance-style former Seoul Station, now a free exhibition hall with rotating art and design shows.
description: Korea's original Seoul Station building, an ornate 1925 brick-and-dome structure, was retired from rail service and reopened in 2011 as a free public exhibition and events space. The restored waiting hall and stationmaster's rooms host rotating contemporary art, design, and history exhibitions, and the building itself - all domes, arches and period detail - is worth the short visit even between shows. It sits right beside the working Seoul Station, easy to fold into a transit day.
highlights: 1925 domed Renaissance-style waiting hall
Rotating free art/design exhibitions

tips: Visit is roughly 30-45 minutes - easy to combine with a Seoul Station transit connection

name: Seoul Metropolitan Library
summary: The old Japanese colonial-era City Hall reborn as a public library, its three-story reading wall facing Seoul Plaza.
description: Seoul's former City Hall (built 1926) was converted into a striking public library in 2012, keeping the historic stone facade while opening a soaring reading room lined floor-to-ceiling with books behind glass. The main hall's stepped 'reading stairs' overlook Seoul Plaza and the modern glass City Hall next door - a genuinely photogenic contrast between old and new Seoul. Anyone can walk in and browse for free; the building alone is worth a quick look even without reading.

name: National Hangeul Museum
summary: A free, modern museum on the Korean alphabet next to the National Museum of Korea, with playful hands-on Hangeul exhibits.
description: Dedicated entirely to the Hangeul writing system King Sejong created, this bright, modern museum sits directly beside the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan Family Park. name: Dongdaemun Doota Mall & Night Shopping
